exposure: Type of intrapartum fetal monitoring (wired CTG, intermittent auscultation)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 861 women who responded to an Australian national survey examining experiences of intrapartum fetal monitoring in labour.
finding: Women monitored via wired CTG were more likely to use pharmacological pain management, have an emergency caesarean section, and felt that monitoring had a negative impact on their labour.
mod_finding: Women monitored via wired CTG were more likely to have an emergency caesarean section, while those who gave birth vaginally were more likely to have been monitored via intermittent auscultation.
cross-section timing: Intrapartum and immediate postpartum (experiences in labour)
